decisions.quote:
Academic and behavior combined support: A single-case practice-based replication study.
Gettinger M, Kratochwill TR, Levin JR, Eubanks A, Foy A.

The purpose of this research was to conduct a practice-based replication of Academic and Behavior Combined Support (ABC Support), a previously developed and experimentally evaluated supplemental intervention that merges a combined focus on reading fluency and academic engagement. In the present study, a school-based interventionist and data collector had access to implementation resources online and participated in virtual training and coaching. Four Grade 2 students received the ABC Support intervention for 6 weeks in their school. Students' oral fluency on training and non-training reading passages, as well as occurrence of engagement and disruptive behaviors during universal reading instruction, were measured repeatedly across baseline, intervention, and follow-up phases in a multiple-baseline design. decisions.reason: The 2024 abstract reports a 4-student Grade 2 multiple-baseline practice-based replication of Academic and Behavior Combined Support (ABC Support), "a previously developed and experimentally evaluated supplemental intervention," finding baseline-to-intervention and follow-up gains in reading fluency and classroom behavior "[i]n concert with prior empirical findings on ABC Support." Across the 49 deposited references (bb0005-bb0245), only two entries concern ABC Support: bb0085 (Gettinger, Kratochwill, Eubanks, Foy, & Levin, 2021, J. Sch. Psychol. 89, 1-19, 10.1016/j.jsp.2021.09.004, shipped row 1563) and bb0090 (Gettinger, Kratochwill, Foy, & Eubanks, 2021 online / 2022 print, Intervention in School and Clinic 58(1), 15-20, 10.1177/10534512211047571). Inspection of both complete primary texts establishes that 10.1016/j.jsp.2021.09.004 (09_gettinger_evaluation.unrepaired.txt) is the sole prior experimental evaluation of ABC Support, testing six Grade 2 teacher-student dyads in a randomized multiple-baseline design and reporting significant gains in standard-passage WCPM (p = .006), training-passage WCPM (p = .001), academic engagement (p = .001), and reduced disruptive behavior (p = .001). Conversely, 10.1177/10534512211047571 (10_gettinger_development.unrepaired.txt) is practitioner implementation guidance (10 elements and 15 steps) with no empirical sample, design, or outcome analysis. While 2024 in-text citation attribution remains unavailable without the 2024 body, Codebook Step 2 uniquely binds target 0 by description to the empirical evaluation in shipped row 1563.
